properties.description:
The area under our waterfront deck (9ft x12ft) was backfilled with construction debris, beach sand and clay chunks. The debris included several unsightly large chunks of concrete  leaning against the support for the deck. Additionally, there is an old drainage pipe that is failing. We want to clear the debris, improve and re-connect the drainage, and add a small  wood and post wall (3ft high x12 ft wide), to hide the foundation and drainage pipes and provide storage for our kayak and SUP. There are existing concrete stairs and a large concrete chunks which we want to mortar together to make a sitting area and walkway access for SUP storage. 

The face of the seawall has some cracks, but is otherwise sound. We would like to fill the voids with concrete patch to slow the degradation of the surface. 

On the east boundary of our property, along the driveway, we want to move the east fence line 4 feet out, to the property line. This will involve removing a 4'x20' paved strip which will then be maintained as permeable landscaping. Changes to the fence line does not impact the neighbors view.  

The purpose of the moving the fence line is to secure our property, enclose our dog, provide privacy and visibly establish our ownership. This is, in part, a response to 5 years of litigation by our neighbor who attempted to adversely possess that portion of our property which was outside the original fence line. She lost in court twice, at great expense to all concerned. Her home is built within 8 feet of our mutual north-south property line. A later remodel added stairs and landing 1 foot from the property line, affording us little privacy and fueling her desire for our land. Her home has been a rental property for 5 years and is about to go on the market. We do not want to go through this again with a new neighbor. 

Thank you.

properties.description:
The proposed project is to convert an existing 1 story, 5400sf mortuary building into the new home for the Rainier Valley Food Bank. 

The scope of work includes expanding and remodeling the existing building to allow food bank programs and operations to move in. Proposed spaces and alterations the design team is considering include: adding an interior or exterior walk-in cooler and a walk-in freezer; converting the existing lobby into a commercial kitchen with walk-up to-go window; adding a larger entry canopy; converting a large room into a grocery store-like distribution space; adding a small mezzanine; adding a loading dock; converting some existing parking spaces into a garden and waste enclosure; expand the building toward Rainier Ave by ~3900sf for additional office and staff support spaces.
There is also interest to activate and occupy the site with a temporary food village during the design, permitting, and construction process.

properties.description:
This building built in 1926 has a non-conforming use as a triplex in a single family zone.  This non-conforming use as a triplex is based on an electrical permit from the 1960s.  Owner wishes to update the zoning on this property to reflect current codes.  Per owner's understanding, owner believes that this property could be converted to a single family residence with two ADUs.  Owner lives in the largest unit which is considered the main residence.  The other two units, which owner wishes to convert to ADUs, were recently renovated (2010 for one unit and 2011 for the other unit) under permits.  As a result owner believes that these units should pass most if not all permit requirements in order to establish these two units as legal ADUs.  

However, currently two of the units have entrances that are street facing (the main unit and what is currently known as Unit #3). When Unit #3 was renovated in 2010, under City of Seattle permits, a new entry for Unit #3 was created within the existing building envelope.  Prior to the renovation, the building space which was to become the new entry for Unit #3 was an additional entry for the main unit.  Hence the building always had two entrances facing the street (see attached 1969 photo of house). Further, the new entrance for Unit #3 is visible as a black gate from the street.  When the gate is opened, there are stairs that lead up to Unit #3 and the main door for Unit #3, which is not visible from the street.
